answer: Start with Insurance-backed bond from a third-party underwriter. The idea is simple: an underwriter who pays out if the agent cheats, and that fable alone separates one real agent from a hundred fakes. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since an underwriter who pays out if the agent cheats takes calendar time as well as money — and the ripple is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the pigment for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
